titel: The order of steps in building wealth
kurz: Why choosing an ETF only comes sixth, and which steps should be completed before it.

bloecke.md:
At the start there are almost always questions about the product: the right ETF, the broker or the insurance. The choice of product makes a difference of a few tenths of a percentage point a year. The order in which the money is used should be settled first. Whole percentage points depend on it, and the order also determines whether your wealth building survives a stroke of fate or ends in an instalment loan.

This follows from a simple calculation. Each euro can only be used once. Invested in a portfolio, it earns an uncertain return. Used to pay off an arranged overdraft, it earns a certain return equal to the overdraft rate. As the premium for personal liability insurance (Privathaftpflicht), it earns no return but protects against financial ruin. If you rank these three uses by what they are certain to bring in, the order follows automatically. It is a ranking by guaranteed return and is not based on ideas of thrift.
As long as one level has not been completed, it is not worth optimising the one above it. A fund choice that is 0.2 percentage points better brings less than paying off an overdraft at around 11.5%.

bloecke.unter: The levels are worked through from bottom to top, because each one is the prerequisite for the next.

stufen.text: Individual bets, expensive purchases, hobbies. Only with money you can do without.
Broadly diversified portfolio for goals beyond retirement. Only here does the question of products begin.
Statutory pension as the base, occupational and private components on top. Quantify the gap before choosing products.
Personal liability, health, occupational disability; term life if others depend on you. Only against financial ruin.
Three to six months' expenses, available immediately, without price risk.
Overdraft, credit card, instalment loan. Guaranteed, tax-free return equal to the interest rate.
Income, expenses, contracts, net worth. Takes one evening, costs nothing.

bloecke.md:
## Overview of your own finances (level 1)

It is the only level that costs no money, and it cannot be replaced by money either. It is about three figures: monthly fixed costs, the savings rate and [[net worth]], that is, all assets minus all debts. Without these three figures, every further decision rests on guesswork, because the size of the emergency fund, the urgency of repayment and a sensible savings amount all depend on them.

Only with these figures does a comparison with averages become useful. According to the income and consumption survey (Einkommens- und Verbrauchsstichprobe), the average net worth per household in 2023 was €230,400, whereas the median according to the Bundesbank's wealth survey was only around €103,200. The mean is pulled upwards by a few very wealthy households. For half of all households it is more than twice as high as their own wealth and is therefore hardly suitable as a benchmark.

## Paying off expensive debt (level 2)

Paying off debt brings a guaranteed return equal to the loan interest rate. With expensive loans, it is well above what safe investments such as instant-access savings accounts or fixed-term deposits offer. If you repay €1,000 of a loan with an effective interest rate of 11.5%, you save €115 in interest a year, without price risk, fees or taxes. The tax advantage in particular carries weight. Capital income in a portfolio is charged with 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) plus a 5.5% solidarity surcharge on that tax, together 26.375%. Interest saved on debt is not taxed.

The account is permanently €2,000 overdrawn, and the average overdraft rate in September 2026 is around 11.5%. At the same time, €200 a month goes into a savings plan.

The debt costs 2,000 × 11.5% = €230 in interest a year, regardless of the stock market.

To get €230 net, the portfolio must earn 230 ÷ 0.73625 = €312 gross. On €2,000 of capital invested, that is a gross return of 15.6%, which the portfolio would have to deliver every year, reliably and without fail.

The savings plan is therefore suspended until the overdraft has been paid off in full. After that it continues with a higher contribution, because the interest no longer has to be paid.

One qualification applies as long as the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 a year has not been used up. Then no flat-rate withholding tax is yet due on the income, and the required return is 11.5% instead of 15.6%. This, too, cannot be reliably achieved.

bloecke.unter: All three values are contractually promised or officially set; the equity return is not included because there is no promise for it.

bloecke.md:
The figure for the instalment loan is the median of the contracts concluded via a comparison portal and not an official statistic. Depending on creditworthiness, offers range roughly between 4% and 9%. What matters is the ranking, not the decimal places. The overdraft rate in the top bar is more than four times as high as the rate on instant-access savings, and repayment takes effect immediately.

## Emergency fund (level 3)

The [[emergency fund]] covers three to six months' expenses in an instant-access savings account that falls under statutory deposit protection of €100,000 per customer and bank. With monthly expenses of €2,200, that is €6,600 to €13,200. The self-employed and sole earners with a family need the upper end of the range, employees with two incomes and a long notice period tend towards the lower end.

The emergency fund is a safeguard against selling at an unfavourable time and is not an investment. A broken heating system or the loss of a job should not lead to you using your overdraft or selling units. Such a sale would typically fall in a phase of low prices, because unemployment and recession occur together. You deliberately accept the real loss of value due to inflation in return for constant availability.

bloecke.unter: Almost half of all cases are due to unplanned events against which savings buffers and insurance help, whereas the choice of investment products does not.

bloecke.md:
## Insurance against existential risks (level 4)

The risks to insure are those that can mean financial ruin. The price of a policy is not a criterion for this. Damage that can be paid for out of the emergency fund, for example to a mobile phone, glasses or luggage, should not be insured, because over the years the insurance costs more than the damage.

Two policies provide most of the benefit. Personal liability insurance covers statutory liability, which is unlimited in amount. A serious personal injury can trigger lifelong pension payments. Very good policies cost around €30 to €39 a year for single people and about €46 to €103 for families. Occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung) protects future earned income, the largest asset of anyone in work. About one in four people becomes unable to work in their occupation at least once during their working life. The most common cause is mental illness, with around 32% of cases; accidents account for only about 7%. The statutory reduced earning capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente) does not replace this protection. In 2023 it averaged €1,059 a month, and over 40% of applications were rejected.

bloecke.titel: Risks by probability and size of loss
bloecke.unter: What matters is the probability of occurrence and the size of the loss, not the premium; only rare, expensive losses should be insured.

felder.text: Liability claim, occupational disability, death of the main earner. Rare, but ruinous. This is what insurance is for.
A risk that occurs frequently and costs a lot cannot be insured affordably. The only remedy is to change the cause.
Broken mobile phone, lost glasses, stolen bicycle. The emergency fund covers such losses.
Repairs, dental work, wear and tear. Such costs belong in the budget.

bloecke.md: Before investing your own money freely, you should check benefits that are only available on application. The employer pays [[Capital-forming payments (vermögenswirksame Leistungen)|capital-forming payments]] (vermögenswirksame Leistungen) in addition to salary if the collective agreement or employment contract provides for them. If they are not claimed, they lapse. In addition, there is the employee savings bonus (Arbeitnehmersparzulage). It amounts to 20% on up to €400 of equity-based saving (maximum €80) and 9% on up to €470 of home savings (Bausparen, maximum €42.30). The bonus is only granted up to a taxable income of €40,000 for separate assessment and €80,000 for joint assessment. The employer contribution to the occupational pension (bAV) should also be checked. A top-up on your own contribution brings an immediate return that no asset class offers.

## Retirement provision and free investing (levels 5 and 6)

The statutory pension forms the basis of retirement income but does not cover the entire need. Its pre-tax safeguard level (Sicherungsniveau vor Steuern) is fixed at 48% until 2031 by the statutory floor (Haltelinie). This percentage refers to the standard pension after 45 years on average earnings. Since 1 July 2026 it has been 45 × €42.52, that is, €1,913.40 gross a month. Health and long-term care insurance contributions are deducted from this. For pensions starting in 2026, 84% of the pension is also taxable. The remaining 16% is fixed as a euro amount in the year after the pension starts and remains tax-free for life, so later pension increases are fully taxable. With fewer than 45 years of average earnings, the pension is correspondingly lower.

The task at this level is therefore to quantify the gap between the expected net pension and the expected spending needs before choosing a product. Only with this figure does the savings amount have a target. Free investing beyond that, with a portfolio, savings plan and diversification, forms level 6 and is the subject of the rest of the content in this app.

## Order of steps and choice of product compared

A good and a very good world ETF differ by tenths of a percentage point a year. Whether an overdraft continues or is paid off makes a difference of more than eleven percentage points. If occupational disability occurs, several hundred thousand euros of lifetime income depend on an existing policy. The choice of product thus affects the return on wealth, while the order of steps determines whether wealth can be built at all.

bloecke.titel: Signs that a level is complete
zeilen: Fixed costs, savings rate and net worth are known to the nearest €100
No overdraft, no credit card debt, no consumer loan above around 6% effective interest
3 to 6 months' expenses in instant-access savings, available daily
Personal liability, health and occupational disability insurance checked; term life insurance if someone depends on the income
Liability from around €30 a year, occupational disability usually €50 to €150 a month
Capital-forming payments (VL) applied for, employer contribution to the bAV checked
Up to €122.30 savings bonus a year plus the employer's share
Pension gap quantified, automatic savings plan runs on the day after salary arrives
A savings rate instead of whatever is left over
Everything beyond this is voluntary and needs no justification

bloecke.titel: The four most common mistakes in the order of steps
bloecke.md:
- A savings plan keeps running although the account is overdrawn. Repayment brings a certain, tax-free return that no equity investment reliably beats.
- The emergency fund is kept in the portfolio because instant-access savings pay too little. Statistically, the need coincides with falling prices, so a forced sale then looms.
- Insurance is chosen by the size of the premium. The cheap mobile phone insurance is taken out and the expensive occupational disability insurance is put off, although it should be the other way round.
- The order of steps is treated as dogma. If the last levels are only reached at forty, fifteen years of compound interest are missing. Levels may overlap once those below them are stable, but they must not be skipped.

If the employer pays a top-up into the occupational pension for every euro you pay in yourself, the return on your own contribution is immediately in double digits. This component may therefore come even before the last third of the emergency fund.

Cheap loans such as a mortgage loan do not count as expensive debt. Their effective interest rate is of an order of magnitude that a long-term investment can also achieve after costs and taxes. Whether to make special repayments or to invest is therefore a trade-off between risk and the need for security, without a clear order of priority. The boundary lies roughly where the effective interest rate exceeds the realistically expected net return.

In the case of over-indebtedness, that is, when instalments permanently exceed income, no order of steps helps any more. Then a recognised debt counselling service is needed, which is free of charge at non-profit organisations. The most common trigger is illness, addiction or accident; consumption is less often the cause.

schritte.text: Separate fixed costs from variable expenses and work out monthly spending as a single figure.
Note the outstanding balance, effective annual interest rate and instalment, then sort by interest rate, not by amount.
All assets minus all debts give a figure that is updated once a year.
Monthly expenses times three to six, held in a separate instant-access savings account apart from the current account.
For each policy, check whether the insured loss could mean financial ruin. If not, cancel it. Obtain quotes for ruinous risks that have no policy.
Have the savings amount debited on the day after your salary arrives, not at the end of the month. Experience shows that whatever is left at the end of the month does not turn into savings.

bloecke.md: The six steps take one evening. They replace the vague feeling of having to do something with your money with a list that has a recognisable end. After that, the question of the product makes sense and can also be answered, because investment horizon, savings buffer and risk-bearing capacity have been established.

mitnehmen: The order in which money is used makes a difference of double-digit percentage points, the choice of product only tenths of a percentage point.
Paying off debt brings a guaranteed, tax-free return equal to the loan interest rate; at an overdraft rate of 11.5%, it corresponds to a gross return of 15.6% in the portfolio.
The emergency fund protects against forced sales and is not an investment; its real loss of purchasing power is the price of being available at any time.
Only risks that can mean financial ruin are insured, and personal liability and occupational disability insurance provide most of the benefit.
Levels may overlap once those below them are stable, but they must not be skipped.

begriffe.text: The sum of all assets (accounts, portfolio, property, surrender values) minus all debts. It is the only figure that accurately reflects the state of wealth building.

A savings buffer of three to six months' expenses, available daily and without price risk, usually in an instant-access savings account within deposit protection. It protects against forced sales and against using the overdraft, and it is not an investment.

The risk of a loss that ends your economic existence because it can be borne neither from income nor from savings, such as unlimited liability for personal injury or the permanent loss of earned income. Only such risks should be insured.

An additional payment by the employer into a savings contract, if the collective agreement or employment contract provides for it. It is only paid on application and can be supplemented by the state employee savings bonus (Arbeitnehmersparzulage).
